sections.normalized_html: Given that [MATH: X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7)] and [MATH: Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.6)] are independent, calculate [MATH: P(X=1 \, \cap \, Y=1).]
sections.readable_text: Given that [MATH: X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7)] and [MATH: Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.6)] are independent, calculate [MATH: P(X=1 \, \cap \, Y=1).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

[MATH: P(X = 1∩Y = 1)|= P(X = 1) ⋅ P(Y = 1).]

Now, since [MATH: X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7),] we have

[MATH: P(X=1) = 0.7, \quad P(X=0) = 0.3,]

and since [MATH: Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.6),] we have

[MATH: P(Y=1)=0.6, \quad P(Y=0)=0.4.]

Therefore,

[MATH: P(X = 1∩Y = 1)|= P(X = 1) ⋅ P(Y = 1); = 0.7 ⋅ 0.6; = 0.42.]

sections.normalized_html: Given that [MATH: X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.3)] and [MATH: Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7)] are independent, calculate [MATH: P(X=0 \, \cup \, Y=0).]
sections.readable_text: Given that [MATH: X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.3)] and [MATH: Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7)] are independent, calculate [MATH: P(X=0 \, \cup \, Y=0).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
By the addition law, we have

[MATH: P(X = 0∪Y = 0)|= P(X = 0) + P(Y = 0) − P(X = 0∩Y = 0).]

Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

[MATH: P(X = 0∩Y = 0)|= P(X = 0) ⋅ P(Y = 0).]

Therefore,

[MATH: P(X = 0∪Y = 0)|= P(X = 0) + P(Y = 0) − P(X = 0) ⋅ P(Y = 0).]

Now, since [MATH: X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.3),] we have

[MATH: P(X=1) = 0.3, \quad P(X=0) = 0.7,]

and since [MATH: Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7),] we have

[MATH: P(Y=1)=0.7, \quad P(Y=0)=0.3.]

Therefore,

[MATH: P(X = 0∪Y = 0)|= P(X = 0) + P(Y = 0) − P(X = 0) ⋅ P(Y = 0); = 0.7 + 0.3 − 0.7 ⋅ 0.3; = 1 − 0.21; = 0.79.]

Example Prompt:
Given that [MATH: X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.3)] and [MATH: Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7)] are independent, calculate [MATH: P(X=0 \, \cup \, Y=0).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
By the addition law, we have

[MATH: P(X = 0∪Y = 0)|= P(X = 0) + P(Y = 0) − P(X = 0∩Y = 0).]

Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

[MATH: P(X = 0∩Y = 0)|= P(X = 0) ⋅ P(Y = 0).]

Therefore,

[MATH: P(X = 0∪Y = 0)|= P(X = 0) + P(Y = 0) − P(X = 0) ⋅ P(Y = 0).]

Now, since [MATH: X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.3),] we have

[MATH: P(X=1) = 0.3, \quad P(X=0) = 0.7,]

and since [MATH: Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7),] we have

[MATH: P(Y=1)=0.7, \quad P(Y=0)=0.3.]

Therefore,

[MATH: P(X = 0∪Y = 0)|= P(X = 0) + P(Y = 0) − P(X = 0) ⋅ P(Y = 0); = 0.7 + 0.3 − 0.7 ⋅ 0.3; = 1 − 0.21; = 0.79.]
